scenes.headline: How VoxelTTO aligns a scene to your poses
scenes.sub: Voxel-aligned Gaussians, and twenty LoRA steps fitted to each scene.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Parsley! When camera poses drift, feed-forward Gaussian splatting fails quietly: input views look fine, new views don't. Here's how VoxelTTO fixes that.

scenes.text: Anchor Gaussians to voxels, not pixels. Then, per scene, train small LoRA adapters until the frozen backbone's cameras agree with your poses.
scenes.say: Two ideas. Anchor the Gaussians to voxels, not pixels. Then, for each scene, fit small adapters until the frozen backbone's cameras agree with your poses.

left.title: One Gaussian per pixel
items: Neighbouring views see the same surface
Overlapping Gaussians leave floaters and shells
left.say: Most feed-forward models make one Gaussian per pixel. Neighbouring views see the same surface, so it gets overlapping Gaussians: floaters and shells.

right.title: Gaussians from a voxel grid
items: Patch tokens fused into one global grid
Each voxel splits into n primitives
right.say: VoxelTTO fuses the backbone's tokens into one global voxel grid, encodes it with a sparse 3D U-Net, and splits each voxel into Gaussians.

scenes.title: Twenty LoRA steps at test time

steps.say: Images climb the frozen backbone, which also decodes a camera for every view.
Adapters go on the query, key and value projections of layers thirteen to forty. Layers one to twelve get nothing.

steps.note: not photometric: rotation, translation and intrinsics
steps.say: The loss isn't photometric. It compares the decoded cameras with the poses you supplied.

steps.note: the Gaussians move because the features move
steps.say: Twenty steps bend the backbone's attention until its cameras agree. The Gaussians move because the features move.

scenes.title: Tanks and Temples: input-to-test view gap
scenes.say: On Tanks and Temples, rotation error falls from one point six three six degrees to point two six two. The view gap shrinks from nine point oh three decibels to one point six six.

scenes.text: TTO doesn't make the model better. It decides whose coordinate frame wins, and it always picks yours.
scenes.say: So the fit doesn't make the model better. It decides whose coordinate frame wins, and always picks yours. If your poses are wrong, it drags the scene onto them.

recap: Gaussians anchored to a voxel grid, not pixels
LoRA fitted to your poses, twenty steps a scene
Test views align; input views can pay for it
scenes.say: To recap: voxels instead of pixels, adapters fitted to your poses, and a trade worth checking against your own cameras.
